title: Sundial Shift — Quickrun Handoff Notes (draft)
content:
Context: quick, pocket-sized handoff for the overnight shift (Sundial). Meant to be read in 2-4 minutes. Not a replacement for formal runbook — temporary fixes + triage notes.

Summary of last 8h:
- 02:10 UTC: short live traffic blip to hosted-api-us-west; p95 latency rose from 120ms -> 950ms for ~9 minutes.
- 03:05 UTC: KV cache eviction event on ded-serv-3 after rolling restart; caused higher rps to CPU path.
- 05:40 UTC: Canary rollout of model-xq-2 auto-fallback triggered (expected) due to GPU OOM on dedicated pool. Auto-fallback worked; no user-facing errors.

What I did (chronological):
- Noted spike in Datadog alert: inference.latency.p95 > 800ms. Opened quick dashboard and validated tail latencies.
- Rolled back recent daemon config on ded-serv-3 (restarted with older NV_DRIVER=520.61).
- Forced small cache warmup: prefetched 50 top-prefixes for common endpoints (see commands below).
- Increased model routing weight to fallback-tier for 6m when ded pool capacity dipped.

Immediate impact: p95 returned to ~130ms after restart and warmup. No errors in user logs. Observed slight increase in token cost during fallback window (~+6%).

Open / followups (to be handled next shift):
- Investigate root cause of KV cache eviction during rolling restart: systemd unit ordering may be racing with GPU drivers. Ticket created: JIRA-8342.
- Add a graceful eviction pause in rollout script for ded-serv nodes (defer restarts until cache sync complete).
- Run a soak test for model-xq-2 ondedicated with simulated peak to reproduce OOM.
- Add warmup hook to canary rollout pipeline (short-lived pre-warm for common prefixes).

Quick triage checklist (TL;DR):
1) Check alerts: Datadog monitor names: inference.latency.p95, serving.kv.evictions, model.router.errors.
2) If p95 spike: verify where traffic routed (query model_router service) -> `curl -s https://console/redwood/api/router/route?map=recent`
3) Check ded pool capacity: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated -o wide` and `kubectl top nodes`.
4) Check KV cache evictions: `curl -s http://obs.local/kv/evictions?node=ded-serv-3` or Datadog tag searches.
5) If cache evictions concurrent with restart, consider restarting systemd units in order: `systemctl stop redwood-gpu-runtime`, wait 10s, `systemctl start redwood-kv-cache`, then `systemctl start redwood-gpu-runtime`.
6) If GPU OOM on a model: shift traffic to fallback variant with routing command below.

Useful commands (copy-paste friendly):
- model routing shift (temporarily): `python tools/route_change.py --model model-xq-2 --set-weight fallback=1.0 --reason \"overnight fallback due to OOM\"`
- warmup common prefixes: `scripts/warmup_prefixes --target endpoint/chat --file samples/top50-prefixes.txt --concurrency 8`
- check recent container restarts: `kubectl get pods -n serving --field-selector=status.phase=Running -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount | grep ded-serv`
- grab last 200 logs for router: `stern router --since 15m --tail 200`

Dashboards & quick links:
- Live latency dashboard: https://datadog.company.com/dashboard/latency-live
- KV eviction panel: https://datadog.company.com/dashboard/kv-evictions
- Router health: https://grafana.company.com/d/router/router-health
- Oncall Slack channel: #infra-oncall (use slack template below)

Slack templates (paste and edit):
- Short incident alert: `@infra-oncall FYI: observed p95 spike on hosted-api-us-west at 02:10 UTC; restarted ded-serv-3 and applied warmup; p95 back to normal. Following up with JIRA-8342.`
- Paging an engineer: `@marco_g urgent: ded-serv-3 showing repeated KV eviction during rolling restarts; could you take a look? Logs: <link-to-logs>`

Temporary mitigations applied during my shift:
- forced fallback to fallback-tier for 6 minutes starting 03:08 UTC (routing script).
- pre-warmed top 50 prefixes for chat endpoint (scripts/warmup_prefixes).
- rolled back a driver upgrade on ded-serv-3 (restarted node with NV_DRIVER=520.61).

Things to watch for next 2 shifts:
- Any recurrence of serving.kv.evictions — if yes, escalate to platform-engineering and attach `journalctl -u redwood-kv-cache` logs.
- Model-xq-2 OOM frequency: if >3 times in 24h, pin traffic to stable-quantized variant and schedule model onboarding review.
- Cost impact from fallback windows — check daily cost dashboard (billing team notified via JIRA if >10% delta).

Sticky notes to self (unresolved):
- Confirm whether the node rollback was necessary or if cache warmup alone would have sufficed (need A/B of similar incident).
- Add more descriptive tags to Datadog monitors (region, pool, model) to aid next triage.

If you're reading this on shift: skim Summary, then Quick triage checklist. If you need me: @aisha_p on Slack, mobile available if incident escalates.

End of notes. Keep it short, follow the checklist, and add updates to this doc (append timestamp + one-line summary).

Recent edits log (manual):
- 2025-09-18 08:12 UTC — created (Aisha)
- 2025-09-19 03:55 UTC — added warmup commands and routing snippet (Aisha)
- 2025-10-03 22:05 UTC — noted driver rollback + JIRA ticket (Aisha)
